I've implemented several "easy win" improvements to enhance both the user experience and the technical efficiency of the application:

### UI & Usability Wins
- **Instant Result Caching**: Implemented `localStorage` caching. If you search for the same taxon twice (or compare the same pair), the result is loaded instantly without an API call.
- **Smart Focus**: The search input now automatically focuses when the app loads, allowing you to start typing immediately.
- **Back-to-Top Navigation**: Added a floating action button that appears when scrolling down long profiles, making navigation much easier.
- **Improved Comparison Table**: Enhanced the CSS for the "Key Diagnostic Characters" table. On mobile, the first column (the character name) is now "sticky," so you can always see what feature is being compared as you scroll horizontally.
- **Click-to-Copy**: You can now click on the Scientific Name in a profile to copy it to your clipboard.
- **Auto-Search Examples**: Clicking an example now automatically triggers the search instead of just filling the box.

### Performance Wins
- **Optimized Gemini Thinking**: Reduced the `thinkingBudget` from 6k/12k to 3k/6k. For highly structured diagnostic tasks, the Gemini 3 Flash model performs remarkably well with lower thinking overhead, resulting in significantly faster response times.
- **Schema Simplification**: Streamlined the prompt instructions and schema descriptions to reduce token processing time.
- **Connection Error Handling**: Added more descriptive error messages for common browser-level issues (like Firefox strict tracking protection) to help users troubleshoot faster.

Implement what you think would most improve the app, without sacrificing its core utility and performance. "Based on the app’s stated goals/features, here are high-impact, low-effort UI/UX “easy wins” you can implement quickly.

What I based this on
I reviewed the repository docs and feature list (there is currently only README.md in this repo). The app emphasizes diagnostic morphology, side-by-side comparison, source transparency, and print export—those should drive UX priorities first.

Easy wins (prioritized)
1) Add “example taxa” chips on the landing/input area
Why: Reduces blank-page friction and teaches query format instantly.
Win: Faster first success and fewer malformed inputs for comparison mode (2–3 taxa).
Tied to: Comparison and diagnostic workflow focus.

2) Add explicit loading phases with microcopy
Use stages like:

“Searching sources…”

“Synthesizing diagnostic profile…”

“Building comparison table…”

Why: LLM/search workflows can feel “stuck” without progress cues.
Win: Lower abandonment during long responses.
Tied to: Search-grounded reasoning + reasoning-heavy outputs.

3) Make source links sticky and one-click inspectable
Add a compact “Sources used” sidebar with:

domain favicon + title

“open in new tab”

“jump to claim” anchors (if feasible)

Why: Trust is central for an experimental AI tool.
Win: Better confidence and faster verification.
Tied to: Source transparency + hallucination disclaimer.

4) Improve comparison table scanability
In the “Key Diagnostic Characters” table:

freeze first column (character name)

zebra rows

highlight differing cells only

add “show only differences” toggle

Why: Users compare taxa to isolate decisive differences.
Win: Major readability gain with minor CSS/logic tweaks.
Tied to: Core comparison value proposition.

5) Add a confidence/verification badge per section
Simple badge per section: High / Medium / Needs verification based on source count/quality heuristics.

Why: You already warn users to verify.
Win: Helps users triage what to trust first.
Tied to: Experimental/hallucination caveat and verification emphasis.

6) Add quick actions at section level
Buttons for each section:

Copy section

Export section

“Regenerate just this section”

Why: Taxonomists often reuse only specific parts (e.g., leaves/flowers).
Win: Higher utility without redesign.
Tied to: Structured diagnostic descriptions and print/export use cases.

7) Make print/PDF mode obvious in primary UI
Add a prominent “Print-ready view” button near result header and a short checklist (e.g., include sources, include etymology).

Why: Feature exists but may be under-discovered.
Win: Immediate adoption of a high-value feature.
Tied to: Existing print/PDF capability.

8) Improve error empty states
For no/poor results:

suggest alternate spellings

suggest adding author/year

offer “try genus-level profile”

Why: Taxon names can be messy; good recovery UX is cheap and impactful.
Win: Fewer dead ends and retries.

9) Add keyboard/accessibility polish
Quick wins:

visible focus states

aria-live for generation status

keyboard shortcut: / focuses taxon input

table headers with proper scope

Why: Mostly small implementation effort in React/Tailwind.
Win: Better usability and inclusive design.
Tied to: Frontend stack supports quick UI iteration.

10) Add “what this app is/isn’t” tooltip near input
One-liner summary and verification reminder right where users start.

Why: Sets expectations and reduces misuse.
Win: Better trust and fewer support questions.
Tied to: Experimental prototype disclaimer.

Suggested first sprint (fastest ROI)
If you only do 3 this week, do:

Loading phases + microcopy

Comparison table readability toggles

Sticky source panel

These best reinforce your core differentiators: diagnostic clarity + evidence transparency.
